fellowship.projectAbstract: Organic photodetectors (OPDs) are an emerging category of optoelectronic devices to convert light (photon) information into an electronic signal, based on photoactive molecules which absorb light. Compared to traditional silicon-based devices, they offer several attractive features such as lightweight, biocompatibility, and easy tunability of absorption wavelength by chemical design of molecules, and they can be utilized in many key emerging applications such as biomedical sensors, environmental monitoring, and automatic driving devices.
